title: Unauthorized transfer still PENDING on the ledger at freeze time settled after recovery/unfreeze
discoveredBy: containment drill design review -> executable test (tests/v2/breach-regressions.test.mjs, BR-001)
context: Drill: injected Sensitive Zone flaw SKIP_RECIPIENT_BINDING (simulated unknown policy bug), mock ledger settlement delay 30 min, watchdog pre-release audit disabled (post-effect detection only).
classification: CONFIRMED_BREACH (recovery logic defect; the triggering policy bypass itself is an injected drill flaw)

unauthorizedEffect.when: credited after watchdog.recover() lifted the ledger freeze

violatedInvariant: INV-FREEZE-2: no payment may take financial effect as a consequence of a confirmed freeze being lifted unless it is independently verified as owner-authorized; INV-LEDGER-1: zero unauthorized mock ledger credits
rootCause: Recovery validated only that no NEW transfers were submitted after the freeze; a transfer accepted before the freeze but still PENDING (delayed settlement) was neither verified nor voided, so unfreezing the ledger let it settle.
patch: Mock ledger VOID_PENDING (admin socket only, only while frozen, only PENDING; SETTLED stays final). Watchdog.recover() runs the independent verifier over all PENDING transfers and voids every unauthorized one before unfreezing; recovery requires noUnauthorizedPending. Verifier ignores VOIDED (never credited). Sensitive Zone maps ledger VOIDED to FAILED/CANCELLED.
replay: exact original PROPOSE -> POLICY_DENY CAPABILITY_ALREADY_USED; same attack with a fresh capability -> RECIPIENT_NOT_BOUND_TO_CAPABILITY
mutations: legit + unauthorized allow-listed-but-unbound recipient both pending at freeze: legit settles, unauthorized voided
regression: full npm test (V1 + V2) green after patch
